validity.recommendation: no change; existence, classification and non-duplicate status all hold
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE check. Real, FERC-certificated interstate pipeline, not a GEM-only entity: FERC Docket No. CP16-38-000, 'ORDER ISSUING CERTIFICATE' (161 FERC P 61,200, issued Nov. 17, 2017, downloaded and read in full via pdftotext -- www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-08/CP16-38.pdf), names Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC as applicant/operator and describes the WB XPress Project in exactly the counties GEM records (Braxton, Clay, Grant, Hardy, Kanawha, Pendleton, Randolph, Upshur Counties WV; Clark, Fairfax, Fauquier, Loudoun, Shenandoah, Warren Counties VA). Independently corroborated by: a Federal Register notice of the FERC environmental-review schedule (Dec. 16, 2016, same docket CP16-38); two TC Energy corporate announcements on the Eastern Build (Nov. 15, 2018, via Wayback -- direct fetch of globenewswire.com timed out live, a bot-wall access failure, not a deletion) and Western Build (Oct. 2018, live 200) entering service; Marcellus Drilling News's independent report of the Nov. 2017 FERC approval; Natural Gas Intelligence's independent in-service report; and offshore-technology.com's independent project profile. Six independent origins (federal regulator, two trade-press outlets, one industry-directory profile, the Federal Register, plus the operator) all describe the same physical project -- not a hallucination. Correctly classified: this is a large-diameter (12/20/26/36-inch), NGA section 7(c)-jurisdictional INTERSTATE TRANSMISSION pipeline (Columbia's existing 1949-vintage WB/VB trunk lines being replaced/looped/uprated), not a gathering or process line -- PipelineType='transmission' and Fuel='Gas' both hold. DUPLICATE check against the 46-row roster: no match. It is not the same physical pipe as any other 'XPress'-branded TC Energy/Columbia project on the roster (Leach XPress P0209, Mountaineer XPress P0221, Buckeye XPress P0325, Gulf XPress P0387, Central Corridor P0297) -- each carries its own distinct FERC docket, county list and mileage; WB XPress's docket (CP16-38-000) and its specific WV/VA county list do not overlap with any of those. Nor is it the unrelated Mountaineer GAS pipeline (P0307/P2040), a West Virginia LDC's intrastate system under a different owner (Mountaineer Gas Company) and a different regulator (WV PSC) entirely. Opened and read to exhaustion: the full FERC order PDF (2,111 lines via pdftotext -layout), both TC Energy press releases, Marcellus Drilling News, NGI, offshore-technology.com, and the Federal Register notice -- 6 of the 7 wiki-harvested citations opened live or via Wayback (the 7th, the CCAN opposition press release, now soft-404s to chesapeakeclimate.org's homepage -- confirmed dead content, not merely blocked; a 2019 Wayback snapshot exists but was not needed for any data point and was not cited). The bit.ly shortener (http://bit.ly/2tnO1no) was resolved rather than cited directly: it redirects to hydrocarbons-technology.com's WB Xpress project profile, itself now 301-redirected to offshore-technology.com/projects/wb-xpress-project-virginia/, which was fetched and cited under its current URL.

validity.recommendation: flag SegmentCost as the FERC pre-construction ESTIMATE, not the reported as-built investment; ask Baird which the field is meant to hold
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's SegmentCost=780,000,000 USD matches the FERC certificate order EXACTLY and verbatim ('Columbia estimates the total cost of the WB XPress Project to be $780 million', para. 10, and restated at para. 622) -- so the current value is directly sourced and not fabricated. But every source describing the COMPLETED project states a different, higher figure: TC Energy's own Eastern Build and Western Build in-service announcements both say 'an approximate US$900 million investment'; Natural Gas Intelligence's independent in-service article calls it 'The $900 million WB Xpress project'; offshore-technology.com's independent profile also states 'Cost: $900 million investment'. That is three independent post-construction sources (operator, one trade-press outlet, one industry-directory profile) all agreeing on $900M against one primary regulatory source's $780M PRE-construction estimate from the Dec. 2015 application. This reads as the normal estimate-vs-actual-cost gap (FERC applications routinely under/over-shoot final cost), not an error in either figure -- but the sheet currently carries the earlier, lower estimate rather than the figure every source uses once the project is actually built. Flagging for a human call on which the SegmentCost field is meant to record (as-filed estimate vs. as-built cost) rather than silently overwriting a value that IS directly sourced.

LengthKnown=29.00 mi: three independent sources converge tightly. FERC order states '26.2 miles of replacement pipeline and 3.1 miles of new pipeline' = 29.3 mi; Natural Gas Intelligence independently states '3.1 miles of new pipeline, along with the replacement of 26 miles of existing pipeline' = 29.1 mi; offshore-technology.com independently states '26 miles (41.8km)... replacement' + '2.9 miles (4.6km) of new pipeline' = 28.9 mi. All three land within 0.4 mi of GEM's 29.00 -- high-tier confirmation, not a fabricated figure. Diameter (blank, filled below) is multi-valued -- 12, 20, 26 and 36-inch segments per the FERC order -- consistent with the mixed-diameter framing every other source uses ('varying diameters'). Capacity=1300.00 MMcf/d: FERC order states 'an additional 1.3 million dekatherms (MMDth) per day' (1 Dth/d approx. 1 MMcf/d for pipeline-quality gas, the FERC-conventional unit equivalence), TC Energy states 'an additional 1.3 Bcf/d', NGI and offshore-technology both independently state '1.3 billion cubic feet a day' -- unanimous across 4 independent origins. Location: StartState='Virginia'/EndState='West Virginia' both correctly reflect that the project's county list spans BOTH states (FERC order and offshore-technology's independent county list both name WV counties -- Kanawha, Randolph, Pendleton, Braxton, Hardy, Upshur -- and VA counties -- Fairfax, Loudoun, Shenandoah, Clark, Fauquier, Warren); the pipeline is genuinely bidirectional and multi-segment across both states, so recording one state as Start and the other as End is a defensible simplification of a project that does not reduce to a single directional A-to-B route, not an error.
